question_text: Puneeth's father went from Lucknow to Kanpur in 2 hours by riding his motorcycle at a speed of 50 km/h. If he drives at 75 km/h, how long will it take him to reach Kanpur? Can we form this problem as a proportion 50 : 2 :: 75 : __?

find.description: can it be solved by direct Rule of Three

solution_steps.description: Explain inverse relation: distance = speed * time.
solution_steps.pedagogical_hint: As speed increases, time decreases! Direct proportion 50:2 :: 75:? is WRONG.
solution_steps.custom_prompt: Can this problem be modelled as direct proportion 50 : 2 :: 75 : __?
accept: No, speed and time are inversely proportional
solution_steps.explanation: No, because increasing speed reduces travel time.
solution_steps.hint_1: Higher speed means shorter travel time.
solution_steps.hint_2: Direct proportion would wrongly increase time.

solution_steps.description: Distance = 50 * 2 = 100 km. Time = 100 / 75 = 1.33 hours (1 hr 20 min).
solution_steps.pedagogical_hint: Total distance = 100 km. Time at 75 km/h = 100 / 75 = 4/3 hours.
solution_steps.custom_prompt: How long will it take at 75 km/h?
solution_steps.explanation: Distance = 50 * 2 = 100 km. Time = 100 / 75 = 4/3 hrs = 1 hr 20 min.
